daily_crawler_accrual_metrics.claim_limit: non_self_originated_requests_count counts requests whose user agent does not match this project's own instrumentation signatures. That is NOT the same as 'requests this project did not make' — it was phrased that way and the phrasing was stronger than the mechanism, which only ever compared user-agent strings and cannot establish who sent anything. It is NOT a crawler count. known_crawler_ua_matches is the only figure this project will describe as crawler access, and only its user agents are published as strings; the rest are counted, not quoted. A recorded user agent is evidence that a request was made and is NOT AN ACCUSATION against the party it names: these strings are self-declared, unauthenticated, and reproduced here as observed data rather than edited to satisfy a prose rule. Every crawler named in this project's PROSE is anonymized; this file is generated evidence and is not.

phase_2_latency_benchmarks.target: Deployed Cloud Run / Vertex AI Agent Path

h6_revocation_cascade_real_corpus_scale.cold_start_note: Front door, rights-custodian AND revocation-worker all cold. The chain is three services deep now, so the pre-flight has to warm more than the front door — a cold hero beat is twenty seconds, not two.
h6_revocation_cascade_real_corpus_scale.note: Re-measured 2026-08-21 after the revocation-route cutover put /api/v1/revoke behind the private worker. Warm rose ~1896 -> ~2652 ms mean (median 2466 ms; the 4642 ms sample is one service waking mid-run and is kept in the set rather than trimmed, because it is a take you can actually get). The full arc: ~519 ms in-process, ~737 ms once the cascade took an execution lease and an idempotency outbox, ~1896 ms once the work-ownership check crossed into the rights-custodian workload, ~2652 ms now that the cascade itself executes in the propagator's own service. Every increase bought a boundary that used to be a promise.

natural_language_license_path.note: Re-measured after the domain split. ~3518 -> ~3926 ms; the added ~400 ms is the same custodian hop, and it is a smaller share here because one server-side Gemini call already dominates this path.

overclaim_lint_coverage.layers: deterministic regex list, then an embedding backstop (src/evidence/semantic_backstop.py, gemini-embedding-001) that can only ADD refusals; with the backstop unreachable, coverage falls back to rejected_by_regex_alone
overclaim_lint_coverage.claim_limit: The lint is a backstop against the exact phrasings it enumerates, not a general paraphrase detector. The STRUCTURAL guarantee is the schema: EvidenceRecord.class has no training-membership value, so the system cannot emit the claim as data. The lint only reduces the chance of it appearing in free text.

failure_tolerance_drill.note: Worker forced into an infinite loop. Server-side time is dominated by the 1.0s supervisor deadline, as designed: detection cannot be faster than the deadline it is waiting on. Quarantine, deregistration and reroute add ~110ms on top. The first run includes a Cloud Run cold start.

defect_ledger.counting_rule: one entry per distinct defect with a distinct fix; a recurrence in a new location is a new entry

buyer_api_license_path.note: Both directions rose (~712 -> ~1675 permitted, ~455 -> ~1591 denied) for the same reason as the cascade: the work-scoping check reads `works`, which now lives in hodi-identity behind the rights-custodian workload. The denial is no longer the fast path — it pays the same hop before it can refuse, which is the correct order: you cannot decide a request about a work without first establishing the work.
